Interface RouteTemplate

All Known Implementing Classes:
UriRouteTemplate
public interface RouteTemplate
A parsed route template: which paths a route matches. The router uses the template as it is given, so a library can bring its own template language: it implements this interface, and declares its routes with its templates, or with a RouteTemplateParser and the text of the templates. The String templates of the route APIs and of the route annotations are URI templates, e.g. /pets/{id}.

A template is immutable and safe for concurrent use: match(String) is called for every request the route is a candidate for.

Routes of different template languages share one route table. The router orders them, and resolves the requests that several of them match, by the facts the templates describe: more literal text first (rawLength()), then fewer path variables (pathVariableCount()), then fewer path variables constrained by a regular expression (patternVariableCount()).

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

  • Method Details

    • expression

      String expression()
      The expression of the template in its language, e.g. for the routes endpoint, the metrics and BasicHttpAttributes.getUriTemplate(HttpRequest). It is for display: it is not parsed again. Templates are equal when they match the same paths with the same variables: implementations define Object.equals(Object) and Object.hashCode(), e.g. on the expression; the router uses them to find the GET routes that have an explicit HEAD route.
      Returns:
      The expression

    • variables

      List<RouteTemplateVariable> variables()
      Returns:
      The variables of the template: every occurrence, in order, an immutable list

    • match

      @Nullable RouteCaptures match(String rawPath)
      Match a path. The input is the raw, not percent-decoded path of a request, without its query, which may have a trailing slash. The template applies the rules of its language, e.g. ignores the matrix parameters of the segments, and matches the complete path. The router calls it for every request the route is a candidate for: an implementation prepares its matcher when it is created, and returns RouteCaptures.of(String, List, List) with its variables().
      Parameters:
      rawPath - The path of the request
      Returns:
      The captures of the variables, not percent-decoded, in the order of variables(), or null if the path does not match. A language that captures one value per name gives that value to every occurrence of the name

    • matchPrefix

      default @Nullable RouteCaptures matchPrefix(String rawPath)
      Match a prefix of a path, as the prefix of a locator route matches: the longest prefix of the path that ends before a slash of the path or at its end, or the root /, that the template matches as it matches a complete path. The input is the raw path of a request, without its query.

      By default, the template matches the path, then the prefixes before each of its slashes, from the longest. A language that finds where a match of the template ends in one pass overrides it, e.g. by matching segment by segment.

      Parameters:
      rawPath - The path of the request
      Returns:
      The captures of the variables, whose path is the matched prefix of the path, exactly as given: the rest of the path follows it after a slash. Or null if no prefix matches

    • mount

      RouteTemplate mount(String prefix)
      Mount this template under a literal path, e.g. the context path of the server or the prefix of a route group. The prefix is literal text, not an expression of the language. The router mounts a declared template once, and an implementation should reuse what it already prepared rather than parse its expression again.
      Parameters:
      prefix - The literal prefix, starting with a slash and not ending with one
      Returns:
      The mounted template

    • requiredPrefix

      default String requiredPrefix()
      A literal every path the template matches starts with: the raw path without its query and without a trailing slash, the path the route index looks up. It is a necessary condition only: the router uses it to skip the templates that cannot match a path, and does not rely on a trailing slash of the prefix. A template without a prefix is a candidate for every request of its method, and is matched for each of them: give the longest prefix the language allows.
      Returns:
      The prefix, starting with a slash, or an empty string when unknown

    • rawLength

      int rawLength()
      The length of the literal text of the template, the first key of the order of routes: more literal text is more specific.
      Returns:
      The length

    • pathVariableCount

      default int pathVariableCount()
      The number of variables of the path, the second key of the order of routes: fewer variables are more specific. By default the path variables().
      Returns:

    • patternVariableCount

      default int patternVariableCount()
      The number of variables of the path constrained by a regular expression, the third key of the order of routes: fewer such variables are more specific. It only orders routes: a request two routes match equally otherwise stays ambiguous. By default the pattern path variables().
      Returns:
      The count
